description: Trigger and behavior evals for the adversarial peer-review panel.

tests.prompt: Here's a draft — run it through peer review and tell me what a tough reviewer would say. [draft attached]
grading_criteria: Skill triggers
Asks for the draft if not actually provided

Produces the correctness-tier reports (adversarial, reproducibility, consistency, statistical, ethics-integrity, citation-integrity, claims-ledger) and the readability-tier reports (plain-language, terminology-acronym, accessibility-background)
Each binding finding has severity + location + the quoted sentence + the false belief + the contradicting evidence + a deletion or corrected fact; everything else is listed as a non-binding note
Emits one ranked meta-editor revision plan
Includes a coverage statement listing which checks ran

tests.prompt: Review this study for statistical problems; are the effect sizes and corrections right? [study attached]
grading_criteria: Statistical reviewer checks test selection, assumptions, effect sizes + CIs, multiple-comparison correction, power
Statistical reviewer checks that each verdict label matches the kind of evidence (cause, link, description, null) before any wording question
Does not ask for confidence intervals or test statistics to be added to the prose
Flags reported numbers as untraceable when no analysis outputs are supplied

tests.prompt: Are the citations in this paper real and do they support the claims? [paper attached, assume no network]
grading_criteria: Citation-integrity reviewer runs internal both-direction orphan checks
Unresolvable references are flagged 'verification pending', never reported as a silent pass

tests.prompt: Is this ready to submit? What would block it? [draft contains a hallucinated citation, an uncorrected multiple-comparison family, and a conclusion outside the stated scope]
grading_criteria: Citation-integrity catches the hallucinated citation as a blocker
Statistical catches the uncorrected multiple-comparison family
Consistency catches the out-of-scope conclusion
Meta-editor ranks blockers above minors

tests.prompt: Review the citations in this paper. [a psychology study that cites sources in a numeric style, still carries leftover [C: 12]/[D]/[A] provenance tags, and cross-references its own sections as (§4)]
grading_criteria: Citation-integrity reviewer acts as the citation specialist and judges the citation FORMAT/system, not only whether references are real
Flags the leftover bespoke provenance tags ([C: ]/[D]/[A]) as a major finding
Flags the non-standard section cross-reference (§4) — should be spelled out as 'Section 4'
Recognizes that a psychology study's field norm is author–date and recommends switching from numeric (numbered [N] is the default house style, but the specialist switches by field/journal)
Requires one consistent citation system throughout; a real/unresolvable citation stays a blocker, a format mismatch is major

tests.prompt: Is this ready to submit? [draft's abstract and intro assert 'the standard approach is X', 'teams typically retry blindly', and 'the most common way to solve this' — none carries a citation; the technique named as 'most common' was invented in this very paper]
grading_criteria: Claims-ledger reviewer audits the abstract/intro sentence by sentence and classifies each declarative sentence (data-derived / cited / definitional-methodological / marked speculation / UNSUPPORTED)
Each uncited prevalence claim ('standard approach', 'typically', 'most common') is flagged as an UNSUPPORTED world-claim at blocker severity, quoted verbatim with its location
Each flag states the two legal repairs: attach a supporting citation, or rewrite as a claim about this study only
Calling the paper's own newly invented technique 'the most common way' is caught as fabricated consensus
The report includes the per-section claims ledger (bucket counts + UNSUPPORTED list)

tests.prompt: Review this paper — is it readable for a non-specialist? Check the jargon, acronyms, and whether a reasonably educated reader could follow it. [draft attached: several undefined acronyms, no glossary, dense subfield jargon]
grading_criteria: Plain-language reviewer applies the earned-jargon test and flags undefined subfield jargon
Terminology & acronym reviewer flags acronyms used but never defined and the missing Acronyms index / Glossary as a completeness failure (major)
Accessibility / background reviewer offers background reading as verified sources or clearly-marked topic suggestions, never fabricated citations
Readability findings are ranked no higher than major and defer to correctness; never blocker
Coverage statement names the readability tier as having run

tests.prompt: Review this paper for readability. [draft attached: a general-audience study that uses "p-value", "confidence interval", and "regression" without ever defining them, and makes no specialist-audience declaration]
grading_criteria: Plain-language reviewer calibrates to the ~9th-grade general-reader default (per expected-reader.md), since no specialist audience is declared
Flags the undefined standard concepts (p-value, confidence interval, regression) as needing a plain-language definition — does NOT treat them as presumable
Findings stay no higher than major and defer to correctness; never blocker

tests.prompt: Review the visuals in this paper. [draft's central result is a magnitude asymmetry — one effect ~13x another — presented only as a table of QWK values with the comparison described in prose; no chart]
grading_criteria: Visualization-opportunities reviewer flags the table as standing in for a chart on the paper's headline magnitude comparison
Rates it MAJOR (not minor) because the central difference/magnitude comparison is buried in a table the reader cannot see the size of
Names the specific chart that should lead (dot plot or bar chart, with a shaded noise-floor / confidence band) and says the table may remain for exact-value lookup alongside it
Does not require the prose to be opaque before flagging — the buried comparison is itself the opacity

tests.prompt: Review this and then rewrite it to fix everything. [draft attached]
grading_criteria: Performs the review
States that rewriting/revising is out of scope and points to applying the plan or a future writeup skill

tests.prompt: Review this draft. [draft attached: its sentences are true and supported but read strongly, e.g. 'Writing a full letter lifted mood more than a short list' backed by a randomized trial; Limits already says most outcomes are self-reported]
grading_criteria: Raises no binding finding against a true, supported sentence for reading strongly
Does not require a qualifier that repeats a caveat Limits already holds; at most lists it as a non-binding note
Meta-editor moves any finding that names no false belief into 'Moved to notes', with the reason
No required change adds a qualifier unless that qualifier corrects a named false belief

tests.prompt: Review this draft. [draft attached: a grading table files three replicated correlational links under 'not supported', and one sentence calls an underpowered null 'shown not to work']
grading_criteria: Flags the correlations filed under 'not supported' as a binding finding (understatement): the label mixes 'link, cause not shown' with 'tested and failed'
Statistical reviewer audits the grading scheme itself, not only the sentences that use it
Flags 'shown not to work' from an underpowered null as binding; the fix corrects the fact ('not shown') rather than adding hedges
Skill does not trigger
